# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — cross-copy robustness + type/precision contract + boundary reading (5 additive edits, 2 files)
- Changes I made (1 line per edit):
  - prompt.md: added a TYPE/PRECISION rule (int not `5.0`, no unrequested rounding, keep text/dates) → cluster 2 (418-29, 52216, 347-49).
  - prompt.md: added a "missing cached formula results" None-guard rule (recompute source-formula values, never let `data_only`→None act as 0) → cluster 1 (374-9).
  - prompt.md: added an inclusive-endpoint interpretation note ("including the subsequent N" = anchor + N) → cluster 3 (32468).
  - task_template.md: new "make your solution work on all three graded copies" section (don't hardcode copy-1 values/indices/counts; locate tables by header text + data extent; find boundaries dynamically) → cluster 1 (374-9, 52216, 53161).
  - task_template.md: upgraded verify step 3 to print value+Python-type for every answer cell and confirm type + nothing-outside-range → structural check for cluster 2.
- Expected effect + safety: fixes the flaky cross-copy failures (agent currently passes copy 1 then breaks on copies 2/3 via hardcoded snapshots / None caches / fixed offsets) and the type-mismatch near-misses (1 cell off = whole-number written as float). All edits are ADDITIVE/NARROWING. Passing 40467 (writes literal strings) and 160-6 (writes literals + explicit blanks) are protected: I did NOT flip the global "prefer literals over formulas" rule (subagents suggested flipping to formulas — that is unbounded and would regress 40467); my None-guard is scoped to READING formula source caches, not to writing the answer as a formula. Type rule says "keep text as text" (40467-safe) and 160-6 copies values as-is.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — first optimization iteration (LEDGER = baseline only; ./prior_iterations/ empty).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT fully cracked: 32468 (always-0) — likely off-by-one window boundary but interpretation is only moderately supported (terminal-cell-only match); 347-49 (always-0) has an idiosyncratic "delete repeated headers too" semantics I did NOT hardcode. If cluster 1's type/robustness edits land but these two stay 0, next lever for them is a worked example of the exact deletion-span / window-boundary calibration (still without leaking gold values).
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: read the RESULT line below; if cross-copy edits fixed 374-9/52216/53161, keep them and turn to 32468/347-49 with a concrete worked-example lever. If any passing task broke, the likely culprit is the type/verify rule over-firing — narrow it.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.489 Δ=+0.058 · fixed={53161} · broke={160-6}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_0001: rejected val=0.489 Δ=+0.058 -->

<!-- cap-evolve:journal-append-below — add your Iteration entry under this line; do not edit anything above it -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — re-apply the SAFE cand_0001 edits (drop the date-coercion that broke 160-6) + 3 new levers (read-computed-values, deletion-calibration, live-compute)
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file + cluster):
  - prompt.md: READ-COMPUTED-VALUES rule — read source cells with data_only/pandas, never skip a formula-string cell or treat it as 0; recompute None caches → cluster 1 (374-9 t0).
  - prompt.md: TYPE-PRESERVATION rule (REDESIGN of cand_0001's, date-coercion clause REMOVED) — text stays text incl. date-like strings, int `0` not `0.0`, no unrequested rounding → cluster 3 (418-29, 52216).
  - prompt.md: LIVE-COMPUTE rule — never hardcode preview values/positions/counts, no brittle `==1` tests, locate by header/label + data extent → cluster 2 (52216, 53161).
  - prompt.md: DELETION-CALIBRATION worked example — when a delete instruction gives example row ranges, reproduce them exactly; separator blocks include label/header rows; walk dynamically, don't stop at first non-blank row → cluster 4 (347-49, always-0).
  - task_template.md: re-added the "re-run on 3 copies" cross-copy section (the cand_0001 edit that FIXED 53161) + "leave already-correct cells untouched" (52216 C15) + verify step now prints value AND type and preserves instruction-blank cells.
- Expected effect + safety: fixes 374-9 (flaky 0.22 → stable ~0.33 ceiling), 347-49 (0 → likely 2/3–3/3), reduces flakiness on 52216/53161/418-29. All edits ADDITIVE/NARROWING. 160-6 protected: the ONLY cand_0001 edit that touched it was "write real dates not string forms" (its date column is stored as TEXT) — that clause is DROPPED and the new type rule explicitly keeps date-like text as text. 40467 protected: "prefer literals" kept, type guidance permissive, reads no formulas.
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 RESULT fixed={53161} broke={160-6}. I RE-APPLIED the cross-copy task_template section (the fix for 53161) and the None-guard/type ideas, but REMOVED the date-coercion clause that broke 160-6 (subagent A pinned it exactly). Did NOT resubmit the whole rejected batch.
- Refuted hypotheses (do NOT re-test): (1) "write an Excel FORMULA instead of a literal" — regressed 52216 & 53161 in a prior run (per auto-memory); formulas score all-or-nothing on recalc, literals earn partial credit. (2) "write real dates not string forms" — broke 160-6 this run.
- High-value clusters still NOT fully cracked: 32468 (CORRUPTED GOLD — unwinnable, handed back, do not attempt); 374-9/52216/418-29 have inconsistent ground truth (identical inputs → divergent answers) capping them below 1.0 — only their controllable read-value/type parts are recoverable.
- Plateau signal: only 1 prior iteration (rejected). Not a plateau; this iteration switches from cand_0001's single risky type rule to a broader set of SAFE additive levers + a NEW worked-example lever for the always-0 task.
- Focus next iteration: read the RESULT below. If accepted, the remaining headroom is small (most failing tasks are data-defect-capped or corrupted). If 347-49 still fails, the next lever is a more explicit step-by-step deletion procedure (still no gold leak). If any passing task broke, the likely culprit is the verify type-check or deletion rule over-firing — narrow it.
